title: llm-prices.com (open source: github.com/simonw/llm-prices) — takes typed token counts (prompt/cached/completion), sortable per-model table with checkboxes, 'Prices last updated' stamp; no tokenizer; warns cross-model comparisons are inexact (verified 2026-09-13)

Helicone /llm-cost — input/output token fields + '300+ AI Model Costs' table at per-1k rates, provider filters, batch-rate variants; no tokenizer, no freshness date. PricePerToken.com — ~300-row Nuxt table, claims 'Updated daily'; no tokenizer
OpenAI platform tokenizer page — still live 2026, client-rendered, covers o200k/cl100k lineage only; community-confirmed lag behind new encodings (e.g. o200k_harmony)

Simon Willison, 'Claude Token Counter, now with model comparisons' (2026-04-20; 224 HN points) — per-model comparison from one prompt is the celebrated feature; Anthropic's own announcement: Opus 4.7 tokenizer maps same input to 'roughly 1.0–1.35×' tokens vs earlier Claude; Willison measured 1.46× on a real system prompt. NOT a Claude-vs-cl100k figure (folklore)

Closest new entrants: holaclaw token-studio (in-browser counter + cost), zatomic.ai/tokens (160+ models), gptforwork.com/tools/tokenizer (GPT/Claude/Gemini/Grok) — none lead with offline/no-key/no-signup positioning

js-tiktoken v1.0.21 (2025-08-09, MIT) — pure JS, no WASM. NEVER import the root (bundles all ranks, 5.6 MB dist/index.js). Use 'js-tiktoken/lite' (~9 KB) + rank modules 'js-tiktoken/ranks/o200k_base' etc. (JS modules exporting {pat_str, special_tokens, bpe_ranks}; no .json export). Measured ranks sizes: o200k_base 2.33 MB raw / ~1.1 MB gzip; cl100k_base 1.04 MB / ~0.5 MB. API: new Tiktoken(ranks, extendedSpecialTokens?), encode(text, allowedSpecial?, disallowedSpecial?) → number[], decode(tokens); TiktokenEncoding = gpt2|r50k_base|p50k_base|p50k_edit|cl100k_base|o200k_base; TiktokenModel union covers gpt-4o/o1/o3/gpt-4.1/gpt-5 families. No byte-identity claim exists upstream

openai/tiktoken openai_public.py — def o200k_harmony() reuses o200k_base's pat_str and mergeable_ranks verbatim, differing only in special_tokens (vocab 201,088; <|return|>, <|channel|> etc.) → plain-text o200k_base counts equal harmony counts; constructible offline via Tiktoken(o200kRanks, harmonySpecialTokens)

OpenAI Help Center, 'Understanding and counting tokens' — verbatim: '1 token is approximately 4 characters. 1 token is approximately three-quarters of a word. 100 tokens are approximately 75 words. These are estimates, not exact counts.' Also: plain-text counts omit message structure, tools, schemas, images, files (help.openai.com 403s plain fetchers; wording via reader render)

OpenAI Cookbook — How to count tokens with tiktoken: tokens_per_message = 3, tokens_per_name = 1, every reply primed with <|start|>assistant<|message|> (+3); 'the exact way that tokens are counted from messages may change from model to model'

Anthropic docs — token counting is API-only (POST /v1/messages/count_tokens); 'The token count is an estimate'; no public tokenizer/library; Claude 4.7+ 'use a newer tokenizer' producing 'approximately 30 percent more tokens' than earlier models (docs.anthropic.com 301s here)

LiteLLM model_prices_and_context_window.json — ~2.3 MB, ~3,900 entries, MIT at repo root (Berri AI, 2023; only enterprise/ excluded), repo pushed 2026-09-13 (maintained: gpt-5.2, claude-opus-4-7, gemini-2.5-pro present). Verified fields: input_cost_per_token, output_cost_per_token, max_input_tokens, max_tokens/max_output_tokens, mode, litellm_provider, cache_read_input_token_cost, tiered *_above_200k_tokens, deprecation_date. Prices are USD per token (gpt-4o: 2.5e-06 in / 1e-05 out)

OpenRouter models API — HTTP 200 keyless; 445 models; per-model pricing: { prompt, completion, input_cache_read, ... } as per-token USD STRINGS, plus context_length (total window) and top_provider.max_completion_tokens — snapshot-time cross-check source only, never runtime

Context-window convention (corroborated by LiteLLM max_input_tokens/max_output_tokens and OpenRouter context_length/top_provider.max_completion_tokens): input and output share one total window; output has a separate cap — fit check = input ≤ maxInput AND input+output ≤ maxInput+maxOutput
